lines: Progressive difficulty hearing low-pitched sounds over 6 months, worsening since conception
The patient returns to the Otolaryngology clinic three months following her prior evaluation for a thyroid nodule with suspicious sonographic features.
She is currently in her second trimester of pregnancy and presents with a 6-month history of progressive difficulty hearing, especially when listening to low-pitched sounds.
She reports that her hearing problems have worsened since conception.
She denies any ear pain, discharge, or vertigo.
- Thyroid nodule with suspicious sonographic features for malignancy (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Thyroid nodule with suspicious sonographic features
- Oxycodone 5 mg PO every 6 hours as needed for chronic back pain
She reports that her mother had similar symptoms at a young age.
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: Laboratory technician.
On physical examination, there is no evidence of external ear abnormalities, and the tympanic membranes appear normal bilaterally.
Weber test lateralizes to the right ear, and Rinne test shows bone conduction to be greater than air conduction in the right ear.
Audiometry confirms conductive hearing loss in the right ear.
